claims.text: Tailoring the elemental balance can promote nanoscale coherent precipitates within a predominantly random solid solution.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates can strengthen lightweight high-entropy alloys.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates can promote formation of a uniformly protective oxide layer.
The proposed precipitate-mediated effects can enable low density, enhanced strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance in the same alloy.
Varying the ratio of lightweight to refractory elements and applying thermal treatment will trigger nanoscale phase segregation and coherent-precipitate formation.
The induced coherent precipitates will form both within grains and particularly at grain boundaries.
Isothermal annealing at 600–800°C permits controlled precipitate nucleation without excessive coarsening.
The structural mediator is nanoscale coherent precipitates formed through subtle segregation of refractory elements.
Impeded dislocation motion increases mechanical strength.
Coherent precipitates act as nucleation sites for a uniform protective oxide film during high-temperature exposure.
A uniform protective oxide film improves corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Lightweight elements lower density, whereas refractory-element content contributes durability.
Relative to the baseline, the tailored alloy will exhibit approximately 10–20% higher tensile and yield strength.
Relative to the baseline, the tailored alloy will have a more stable passivating oxide layer and superior corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The tailored alloy will maintain a lower density while improving the other targeted properties.
Excessive precipitate coarsening causes loss of coherency and formation of brittle phases.
Excessive phase separation will deteriorate mechanical properties or protective-oxide integrity.
